conditional_separable_projection_theorem: Consider a finite exact-real inequality system with retained coordinates y and selected scalar coordinates x_j. Require every inequality to involve at most one selected x_j, and every retained equality to have zero coefficient on all selected coordinates. Include the selected coordinates' explicit finite lower and upper bounds as rows before partitioning. This is a conditional hypothesis, not a claim about any selected columns in this problem.

For one selected coordinate write each incident row as a_i*x_j+r_i(y)<=b_i. A positive a_i gives U_i(y)=(b_i-r_i(y))/a_i; a negative a_k gives L_k(y)=(b_k-r_k(y))/a_k. All zero-selected-coordinate rows remain unchanged. For every positive/negative pair retain (-a_k)*r_i(y)+a_i*r_k(y)<=(-a_k)*b_i+a_i*b_k. Both row multipliers are strictly positive, and the selected coefficient cancels exactly.

These pair rows are equivalent to L_k(y)<=U_i(y) for every pair. Thus the real projection is exact: a retained y satisfies all projected rows if and only if every selected coordinate has a nonempty real interval [max L,min U]. Since no source row contains two selected coordinates, choices from those intervals can be made independently. This theorem gives neither existence of any projected y nor a finite-valued extension.

With p_j positive and q_j negative incident rows, and M0 rows involving no selected coordinate, the source augmented row count is M0+sum(p_j+q_j), whereas direct pair generation gives M0+sum(p_j*q_j). Counts include the explicit selected-coordinate bounds; this is not a comparison to a source matrix that omits bound rows. Pair counts are before any additional independently proved redundancy reduction.

Because the explicit finite bounds imply p_j>=1 and q_j>=1, a column's direct pair count does not exceed its incident source count exactly when (p_j-1)*(q_j-1)<=1. For integer counts this requires one side to have a single row, or both sides to have two rows. This is only a symbolic counting criterion; no column has been found to satisfy it. Net growth across a set must be computed from the full sum, and even nonincreasing row count would not establish runtime, conditioning or feasibility.

If source-row support sizes including the selected coordinate are s_i and s_k, a generated pair has at most s_i+s_k-2 retained coefficient positions before exact cancellation. A defensible implementation needs explicit upper bounds on total pair slots, rational bit growth, stored bytes and the cost of independent arithmetic and return checks. These bounds have not been established for any concrete target set.
